title: Shanghai's Nanjing Building digital twin (Huangpu District with Huawei) alerts a guard to an opened third-floor window; a sensor, not AI, detected it and the anecdote carries three dates
summary: A Huawei-hosted launch on 25 Feb 2021 presented a window-opening alert sent to a guard's wristband. Knews and Jiefang Daily say that a window sensor detected it; the story is retold with three dates.
account: The OECD AI Incidents Monitor record 2021-02-25-adca says that Shanghai, with Huawei, launched an AI-powered digital twin in the Nanjing Building that 'detected a high-risk behavior (open window), alerted security, and enabled immediate intervention'. The underlying anecdote appears in Eastday (reporter Xue Ningwei, 25 Feb 2021, via Sohu): during Spring Festival a customer on the third floor opened a window and held a phone out to photograph Nanjing Road, and a guard arrived to stop it; Eastday says that how the guard knew was 'revealed at today's launch', the 'Shanghai city minimum management unit digital governance' release held at the Huangpu District city operations center, which smartcity.team (1 Mar 2021) records as hosted by Huawei Technologies. Jiefang Daily (7 May 2021, via GMW) retells the same window scene during the May Day holiday naming guard Fan Tianyu, and Banyuetan/Xinhua (reporter Zhou Lin, 6 Jul 2021, via The Paper) retells it during the Dragon Boat holiday with the same guard and wording, so no single date can be fixed; the Cyberspace Administration of China repost (4 Mar 2021) phrases it conditionally ('if a visitor opens a window...'). The only witnessed detection was a Knews reporter's deliberate 'open window' test at the launch, where Huawei engineer Chen Tao also simulated smoking for the camera algorithm. Both Knews and Jiefang Daily say that a window-mounted sensor detected the opening and pushed an alert to the guard's wristband through the digital twin; the AI algorithms described (20-plus per Knews and Jiefang Daily, 50-plus per Eastday) run on the 170-plus cameras for smoking, crowd flow and bike parking. Jiefang Daily reports 995 door/window alerts from January to May 2021 and quotes an official that over 80% were triggered by visitors trying the IoT devices. The building is Huawei's flagship store. No harm occurred and no beneficiary is identifiable. The deployment itself (Huangpu District and Huawei, built January 2021; 17 device categories, 80-plus sensor sets, 170-plus cameras) is well documented; the earlier verifier found no English-language report and could not read the CCTV-2 segment. The system's zhiding.cn copy is marked 'industry-supplied copy'.
purpose: The digital twin was built to monitor the building's 'vital signs' (vibration, smoke, lifts, crowd flow, open windows) and push alerts to staff; window opening was named at the launch as a falling-object risk the system flags.
system: Nanjing Building 1:1 'living' digital twin on Huawei Cloud: 80-plus IoT sensor sets in 17 categories, 170-plus cameras, and 20-plus (Knews, Jiefang Daily) or 50-plus (Eastday) AI algorithms for smoking, crowd-flow and parking detection
developer: Huawei (Huawei Cloud, big data, AI, edge computing) with Huangpu District government under the Shanghai City Operations Management Center
deployer: Huangpu District City Operations Center and the Nanjing Building's operator (the Huawei flagship store)
location: Nanjing Building, Nanjing Road East at Henan Road Central, Huangpu District, Shanghai, China
segment: Smart-building monitoring under Shanghai's 'one network to manage all'
taxonomy_note: Loose fit; the detection is attributed to a window contact sensor routed through the digital twin, and the anecdote is a launch vignette.

ratings.reason: No pedestrian was shown at risk and no falling object occurred; the only documented trigger was a reporter's test, so no outcome is documented.

Jiefang Daily reports 995 door/window alerts handled in January to May 2021 but says that over 80% were visitors trying the devices and that real events were far fewer; no efficiency measure is given.

ai_role.statement: For the window alert the sources document a window-mounted sensor whose signal passes through the Huawei Cloud digital twin to a guard's wristband; Knews and Jiefang Daily both say so, and neither attributes the detection to an AI algorithm. The 20- to 50-plus AI algorithms described run on cameras for smoking, crowd flow and bike parking, and the one smoking alert shown at the launch was simulated by a Huawei engineer. The Monitor's statement that an AI system 'detected a high-risk behavior (open window)' is therefore unsupported by its own sources; the earlier verifier reached the same finding.

headline: Huawei digital twin's window alert comes from a sensor, not AI
metric: 995 door/window alerts from January to May 2021

later.note: Jiefang Daily reported that from January to early May 2021 the digital twin had logged 995 door/window alerts, 439 smoking alerts and 55 fire-lane obstruction alerts, while an official said more than 80% of the handled events were triggered by visitors trying the IoT devices.
later.quote: 从今年1月至今，南京大楼“数字孪生”已积累超过50万条数据，处置吸烟告警439次、消防通道阻挡55次、开门开窗告警995次。不过据相关负责人透露，这些处置的事件中，超过八成都是参观者体验物联设备时所触发的，真实事件远没有数据体现得那么多。
